captions.text: In Responder, open Shifts from the navigation, then choose Today.
Across the top are My Shifts, Calendar, Trades, On Duty and Approvals.
Start by reading the intended day card.
Here, A Shift at Firehouse 51 runs from eight in the morning
until eight the next morning.
The words next day matter when planning an overnight handover.
Assigned describes this schedule's assignment mode.
You are on identifies the signed-in person's roster membership, and Fully
staffed is the displayed coverage result.

scenes.title: Search and compare the standby result

captions.text: Use Search shifts to narrow the list.
Entering Community leaves the Community standby signup card.
Read its date and its eight-to-noon time range.
This card shows Sign-up and Approval required, while the current
account already shows You are on.
Those labels answer different questions: how this shift is offered, whether
approval is required, and whether this person is already on its roster.
Searching changes what you see in the list; it does not
change the saved assignment.

scenes.title: Read the day detail and approval rule

captions.text: Open the standby card to read its day detail.
The heading and date identify the selected occurrence, and Scheduled
for repeats its time range.
The page explicitly says that sign-ups and trades on this
required_labels: Sign-ups and trades on this shift need supervisor approval.

captions.text: shift need supervisor approval.
required_labels: Sign-ups and trades on this shift need supervisor approval.

captions.text: Read that rule before planning a coverage change.
Open needs shows Firehouse 51 as Filled, with No role requirements
for this particular day.
Request trade and Add person are visible actions here.
This walkthrough is inspecting the saved day, so neither action is submitted.

visual_required_labels: Sign-ups and trades on this shift need supervisor approval.

scenes.title: Read names, groups and roster source

captions.text: Scroll through Roster and compare the person with the
group and role beside them.
Wallace Boden appears under Command with Chief, while the Engine and Squad entries
identify their own people and roles.
The repeated Scheduled label describes the saved roster source.
Use these details to check that the people and functions
you expected are represented.
Confirm actual availability and attendance through your department's
procedures before assigning work based on this schedule.
Return to the shift views and choose My Shifts.
Under Shifts I am on, the A Shift summary shows its code, personnel
count, group count, next displayed day, rotation and Assigned label.
Scroll to the standby summary to compare its own code and time range.
It shows Manual, Sign-up and Approval required.
Upcoming days begins a separate section below these summaries.
Keep the shift definition and the dated occurrence distinct when
checking which day you need to open.

scenes.title: Filter the calendar and select a date

captions.text: Choose Calendar to look beyond the current day's list.
The month heading establishes the period you are reading, and the filter row
offers All Shifts or an individual shift.
Select Training, Academy signup practice,
then select the twenty-seventh of October.
The legend identifies My shifts, Open slots and Fully staffed.
The selected date appears above its day card, which shows the practice
shift from one until three in the afternoon with two open slots.
This recorded date is historical; its open-slot label does not establish
a current signup opportunity.

scenes.title: Inspect the group's role needs

captions.text: Open that practice day to read the actual group requirements.
Open needs shows Firehouse 51 with Open, two, and a Chief
requirement marked Needed, two.
Below it, Roster says No one is on this day yet.
required_labels: No one is on this day yet.

No one is on this day yet.

captions.text: Compare the required function with the saved roster before
deciding how to fill a gap.
Add person is visible, but this inspection does not change the roster.
Checking the dated requirement helps a supervisor distinguish an
uncovered function from a day that simply has a familiar shift name.

visual_required_labels: No one is on this day yet.

scenes.title: Read the On Duty roster carefully

captions.text: Return to the views and choose On Duty.
A Shift shows ten on-duty entries in this recorded state.
Each entry gives a name, group and role, an Until time and
a Scheduled source label.
Read the shift heading with the individual row so you do not
mix two overlapping schedules.
This view makes the saved coverage picture easier to review.
Its Scheduled entries still need the appropriate availability and attendance
checks for your department's real work.

scenes.title: Inspect the trade and approval queues

captions.text: Choose Trades to review the trade workspace.
This account currently shows No shift trades, and explains that requests
you send or receive appear here.
Then choose Approvals.
The recorded result is Nothing to approve, with a note that sign-ups and trades
waiting for your approval appear here.
These are the current account's displayed queues.
An empty queue is not a completed approval or a confirmed replacement.
Read the actual pending entry and its result whenever your department
performs those operations.

visual_required_labels: Trade requests you send or receive appear here.
Sign-ups and trades waiting for your approval appear here.

scenes.title: Apply the coverage checks to your team

captions.text: Return to the intended day and recheck its identity, hours, personal roster
label and approval requirement.
The same checks help community paramedicine and mental health teams plan
outreach coverage, search-and-rescue teams review mission support, security companies
check a staffed post, wildland contractors plan crew coverage, and industrial
response teams review an emergency roster.
Fire and EMS departments can use them for their own station coverage.
Match your department's roles and dates, investigate gaps, and verify
the actual people before relying on a schedule for a handover.
